newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Canada offers to lead multinational force in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Canada offers to lead multinational force in Zaire.

text.p: Canada on Monday offered to lead a proposed multinational force to help end the crisis in eastern Zaire, according to senior sources at the United Nations.
Canada's ambassador, Robert Fowler, offered the troops at an informal meeting at the United Nations, thereby making the likelihood of a force more probable, the envoys said.
The sources, however, said while Canada had offered to make a substantial contribution, its troops coupled with those offered by France and Spain, would not be enough.
"We will need other contributors, notably the United States," said a senior diplomat, adding that he believed the Canadians would also want Washington's participation.
The U.N. Security Council early on Saturday asked members to lay the groundwork for such a force but did not authorise it until its aims and participation were clear.

Canada has also fielded the U.N. special envoy for the region, Raymond Chretien, its ambasador to Washington and nephew of Prime Minister Jean Chretien. He is currently in the region seeking support for such an intervention to get food to Rwandan refugees who fled fighting in eastern Zaire.
